data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clear paired leaves at each node along the stem, visible in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves spaced along the stem with visible internodes, not clustered at tips)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (each leaf unit consists of multiple leaflets attached to a common petiole)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): even-pinnate (leaflets arranged in pairs along the rachis with no terminal leaflet, visible in close-up images)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 4 (each compound leaf has two pairs of leaflets, totaling four leaflets per leaf unit)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): opposite (leaflets arranged in pairs along the rachis, with two leaflets per node)

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no visible teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering toward both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapering to a narrow base)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein running from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off and curving toward margin)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, 4-6 pairs per leaflet (clearly visible in close-up images, running parallel to margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface reflects light, indicating a waxy or glossy cuticle)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, connecting leaflets to rachis without elongation)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (round and cylindrical in cross-section, no wings or grooves)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and slightly rigid, with visible nodes and internodes)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: green (young stem is green, transitioning to brown in older sections)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no visible ridges or lenticels; surface appears uniform)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate visible upon stem damage or breakage)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaflet base, not characteristic of Fabaceae)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no modified stems or leaves functioning as tendrils)

F. Notes: Some leaflets show minor damage with small holes or margin irregularities, likely due to environmental factors. The plant appears to be a young seedling with multiple stems emerging from a common base. The compound leaves with even-pinnate arrangement and shiny elliptic leaflets are consistent across all images. No flowers or fruits are visible.
